decisions.decision: Box supports div, span, section, article, main, nav, aside, header and footer, with div as default. Forms, lists and tables retain native HTML or dedicated components.

Box exposes parent-layout placement through the shared responsive interface: flexBasis, flexGrow, flexShrink, alignSelf, justifySelf, gridArea and grid row/column placement. These affect the outer host.
Box defaults to inline display for as=span and block display for its eight other supported native tags. An explicit display value overrides the default, so changing as may change layout.

For Box visual value inputs, match Chakra by accepting theme tokens and valid explicit CSS values for colors, corners and shadows. This does not adopt all Chakra props, aliases, opacity shorthand or pseudo-state objects.

findings: Radix Box CSS forces display:block independently of div/span as. Its display enum includes contents; house wrapper-box rule excludes contents.
Radix full layoutPropDefs source supports flexible CSS placement values and responsive objects; house names and band syntax remain separately selected.

candidateRules: Shared CSS styling properties use C-RESP; as and naming references do not become responsive.
Optional styling inputs default to absent, avoiding declarations that defeat consumer CSS. Document browser/default generated-reset effects separately from input getter defaults.
Proposed Box display values are none, inline, inline-block and block, preserving the real-wrapper-box rule. The user-selected default follows as; no contents option.
Spacing uses the selected scale and valid property-specific CSS; negative-token behavior remains open rather than silently inferred from the positive scale.
Dimensions, placement and positioning follow their corresponding CSS value grammars; margin/inset auto remains valid where native CSS permits it.
Visual properties use category-appropriate house theme tokens or valid CSS; exact color/radius/shadow token identifiers remain to specify.
Parent-placement properties reach the outer host. The complete distribution of dimensions/surfaces/internal layout between host and native element remains to verify.
Logical border sides/corners are proposed from the selected logical-name rule and reviewed Pro border usage; this list is not separately approved.
Background images/gradients, transforms and other uncommon declarations remain available through ordinary CSS under the selected focused scope; exact CSS-part contract is open.
